title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans Auditorium on 1969-06-27
lineage: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > DAT > DAT > ZA2 > Soundforge > .wav > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: A solid soundboard capture of the rare 6/27/69 Santa Rosa show, highlighted by Slewfoot, Dire Wolf (Bobby on vocals) and a trippy Dark Star > St Stephen > The Eleven.
ai_review.review: The recording is a generally clear sound‑board source with only occasional hiss and a few mix quirks on the rare “Slewfoot” cut. Musically the concert swings from laid‑back country numbers to a soaring psychedelic second set, delivering standout performances of Slewfoot, Casey Jones (early version), Dire Wolf with Garcia’s pedal steel, and an expansive Dark Star > St Stephen > The Eleven sequence. While Bill’s timing slips on “Dupree’s” and the drums are a bit loose at the very start, the overall energy and variety make this a must‑have for any 1969 Dead collector.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and praise both the performance (especially Dark Star, Slewfoot and Dire Wolf) and the recording’s clarity; minor flaws are noted but do not detract from overall enjoyment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall with good balance; occasional hiss, a few mixing glitches on Slewfoot and early‑show drum imbalance, but generally crisp and listenable.

standout_songs: Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven
It’s All Over Now Baby Blue
show_quality.setlist_flow: First half is relaxed, country‑leaning material; second set erupts into psychedelic jams with a seamless Dark Star > St Stephen > Eleven transition, showcasing the band’s dual folk/psychedelic identity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Featured heavily on pedal steel for Slewfoot, Dire Wolf and early Casey Jones; praised for tone and creativity.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a strong Lovelight section in Dark Star; occasional timing slip mentioned early in the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Takes lead vocals on Dire Wolf, delivering an enthusiastic performance that many reviewers cite as a highlight.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s atmospheric organ/keyboard work is referenced ("drippy chords") adding to the psychedelic texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart sound loose on the opening tunes but lock in strongly for the later jams; Bill noted losing time on Dupree's.
